name: AtariAge POKEY demos -- parallel-stream player
note: The player behind 58 images in the library and 27 different titles --
Arkanoid, Donkey Kong, the Mario Bros sound demos, the AtariAge jingle.
Found by fingerprinting every cartridge's audio-write code and looking
for what recurs, rather than by picking a game and reading it.
Four voices, each with two parallel byte streams: one pitch and one
duration per note, in separate arrays, read through pointers that advance
together. A zero in the duration stream ends the part. Nothing is packed
into bitfields, and there are no patterns -- it is a flat list per voice.
The envelope is a linear decay of the whole AUDC byte. POKEY keeps volume
in the low nibble, so subtracting one from the byte fades the note; how
often comes from a table indexed by the note's own duration, which makes
long notes fade slowly and short ones fast.
_voices_at: Five parallel tables, one entry per voice: the AUDC the voice starts a
note at, and the low and high bytes of its two stream pointers.
Addresses are for the 16K images, which are all of them.
_decay: Frames between one decrement of AUDC and the next, indexed by the note's
duration. Entry 0 is unused because a duration of zero ends the part.
